name: Damask rose (Rosa damascena) extracts and rose oil
short: Reviews: headache, nausea, vomiting, sneezing reported by 2 of 10 trials (inhaled, oral); mild allergic rhinitis by 1 of 11 (oral, skin). Cited capsule trial abstracts give no adverse-event numbers.
text: By mouth or on the skin: a 2022 systematic review of 11 randomised trials of Rosa damascena products taken by mouth (7 trials) or applied to the skin (4 trials) for acute pain reports that one study found mild allergic rhinitis as an adverse effect; the abstract does not say which route that study used. Inhaled or by mouth: a 2021 systematic review of 10 randomised trials of rose aromatherapy or rose taken by mouth for sleep in adults reports that two trials found adverse effects, including headache, nausea, vomiting and frequent sneezing; the abstract does not say which route or product caused them. By mouth in children (a syrup of rose petal extract with brown sugar, a different product from the capsules on the pages): in a double-blind randomised trial in 100 children with constipation compared with polyethylene glycol, the only adverse effect found in the rose group was a bad taste, because the syrup was too sweet. On the skin: in a trial in 120 women with pregnancy-related low back pain, rose oil in almond oil applied for 4 weeks reduced pain intensity, in the authors' words, without any significant adverse effect. By mouth: the cited trials of rose extract capsules for menstrual pain (92 students, compared with mefenamic acid), rose oil soft capsules made with sesame oil for reflux (70 people, compared with omeprazole) and rose extract capsules in 82 menopausal women give no adverse-event numbers in their abstracts; their authors' statements that rose has no side effects or is well tolerated are not backed by event data in the abstracts. A 2016 Cochrane review of dietary supplements for dysmenorrhoea, which included damask rose, found that very few studies reported adverse effects and that evidence of safety is lacking. Combinations: the abstracts of the trials of damask rose with myrtle in capsules and of a four-herb Unani powder containing it report no adverse-event data, so these sources do not cover those products. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
